title: Run the git_utils test scripts through sh so a concurrent fork cannot fail their exec with ETXTBSY
description: Run the git_utils test scripts through sh so a concurrent fork cannot fail their exec with ETXTBSY
no_spec_change_rationale: Test harness only: two git_utils unit tests exec a script they just wrote, which Linux can refuse with ETXTBSY while another test thread forks. Running the script through sh changes no public behavior, requirement or spec text.
acceptance_criteria: Every test that runs a script it just wrote stops holding a write descriptor to that file at exec time: the three that exec their own script run it as `sh <path>`, and the three that put a fake `gh` on `PATH` write it from a child `sh` process. Assertions are unchanged.

In a `rust:1.89` Linux container, 300 rounds of each affected test group (`git_utils::tests`, the bounded-runner tests in `change_tests`, `github::tests`, and the `issues` integration tests) fail 0 rounds with the change. `git_utils::tests` failed 9 of 300 on main 884a33d3.
No gate, timeout or assertion is loosened.
